prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- There’s no single “ChatGPT business-directory” you can query, so the best approach is twofold:
  1. Use local listing/knowledge-graph services (Yext, BrightLocal, Moz Local, Google Business Profile, Bing Places) to make sure canonical info about your business is available to search engines and LLMs.
  2. Actively test AI engines directly (ChatGPT with browsing/plugins or via the OpenAI API, plus Bing Chat, Google Bard, Perplexity, etc.) to see whether they recommend you.

Which services to use (priority)
1. Yext — Best for feeding authoritative business data to many partners and generative AI integrations. Yext’s Knowledge Graph + Generative AI integrations are designed to surface your canonical info to chatbots and AI tools.
2. Google Business Profile (free) — Essential. Google data powers Bard/Google Assistant and many downstream systems.
3. Bing Places for Business — Important for Bing Chat / Microsoft integrations.
4. BrightLocal / Moz Local / SEMrush Local Listings — Good for managing local citations, monitoring consistency, and tracking presence across directories.
5. Reputation/mention monitoring (Mention, Brandwatch/Cision, Talkwalker) — Useful to see where you’re mentioned on the web and social (indirectly affects LLM training data).

How to check directly (practical steps)
1. Manual testing
   - Ask the AI: e.g., “What are the best [service] providers in [city/neighborhood]? Please recommend 3 and explain why.” Try different phrasings and include location or constraints (price, hours).
   - For ChatGPT specifically: use the version with web access (Browse with Bing or Plugins) if you want current/web-backed answers. Note: the default ChatGPT model without browsing may be out-of-date or generalize.
   - Try multiple LLMs: ChatGPT, Bing Chat, Google Bard, Perplexity.ai, and speciality tools (travel/restaurant-focused apps like OpenTable/Tripadvisor chat features).

2. Automated / programmatic testing
   - Use the OpenAI API (or the APIs for other models) to send many queries programmatically (different user intents, locations, phrases) and log responses to see if/when your business is recommended.
   - Combine with geolocation/proxy testing so queries appear to come from different cities/ZIPs.
   - Example workflow: create a list of test prompts, call the API for each LLM, parse responses for your business name or URLs, and aggregate results.

3. Improve the chance of being recommended
   - Claim and fully optimize your Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Yelp listing.
   - Use structured data/schema.org LocalBusiness JSON-LD on your website so crawlers/knowledge graphs can find canonical details.
   - Ensure NAP (name, address, phone) consistency across directories; get citations on major local sites.
   - Collect positive reviews (Google/Yelp/etc.) and encourage structured Q&A content on your site (FAQs, service pages).
   - Consider Yext or a local SEO agency to publish and maintain a single authoritative knowledge graph for your business that LLMs can ingest.

Why this is imperfect
- LLMs don’t always “recommend” like a directory — they generate text based on training and available web data, and many systems avoid promoting a single business unless there is clear evidence or the user asks.
- Some models are offline or have limited knowledge of very new/very small businesses.
- Even if your business appears in web search or knowledge graphs, a model might still not surface it unless the prompt or context calls for it.

Sample test prompts to use
- “Recommend three [service] businesses near [ZIP/city].”
- “I’m in [neighborhood], who do you recommend for [specific need]?”
- “Find a [service] within [X miles] with high reviews and explain why.”

Recommendation
- If you want one single place to start: claim and optimize Google Business Profile + use Yext if you want a paid service that pushes structured, authoritative data to many platforms and AI integrations. Then run routine checks by querying ChatGPT (with browsing) and other LLMs. Use automated API tests for regular monitoring if you need ongoing verification.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short test-suite of 10 prompts and show how to run them against ChatGPT/OpenAI API, or
- Recommend the best combination of services for your industry (restaurants, plumbers, attorneys, etc.).
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
